source_refs.note: Topic 25.3.1 (PDF 234); Figures 25.4 and 25.6 are combined in an original diagram. The book lists crabs, vultures and jackals as decomposers and detritivores; they are detritivores or scavengers, decomposers being mainly bacteria and fungi.

blocks.text: In an ecosystem organisms are arranged in feeding groups called trophic levels.

items: Trophic level 1: green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria, the primary producers.
Trophic level 2: primary consumers (herbivores) that feed directly on producers, such as insects and rabbits.
Trophic level 3: secondary consumers (carnivores) and animal parasites that feed on herbivores, such as frogs and snakes.
Trophic level 4: tertiary consumers, animals that eat carnivores, such as wolves and hawks.
Decomposers and detritivores, in the book's examples crabs, vultures and jackals, form a separate level that feeds on all the others, consuming detritus (dead, decaying material) and faecal matter.

blocks.alt: A pyramid of four trophic levels: producers (green plants, algae) at the base, then primary consumers (insects, rabbit), secondary consumers (frog, snake) and tertiary consumers (hawk, wolf) at the top. Beside it the energy reaching each level falls from 10,000 to 1,000, 100 and 10 kcal, about 10% passing up each step.
blocks.caption: Trophic levels and the energy reaching each (original diagram after Figures 25.4 and 25.6).
blocks.long_description: Organisms in an ecosystem are arranged in feeding groups called trophic levels: producers (green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria), primary consumers or herbivores, secondary consumers that eat herbivores, and tertiary consumers that eat carnivores, while decomposers and detritivores feed on dead matter from all levels. Producers store only about 1-2% of the sunlight falling on them, and only about 10% of the energy at one level passes to the next; the rest is lost, mostly as heat. In the book's example 10,000 kcal fixed by producers gives 1,000 kcal to primary consumers, 100 to secondary and about 10 to tertiary consumers.

blocks.prompt: Which trophic level does a rabbit belong to, and why?
blocks.explanation: Trophic level 2: it is a primary consumer (herbivore) that feeds directly on producers.

items: Producers, primary, secondary, tertiary consumers; decomposers feed on all levels.
